[[Kashmiri cuisine]] consists of a wide variety of dishes, listed below. 

== Barbecue ==

[[File:Sheekh Kebabs.jpg|thumb|''Tujji'' and Kababs.]] [[File:Kabab wazwan.jpg|thumb|Kashmiri kababs can be eaten as a snack or a meal with rice.]]
[[File:'Seekh-Kabaab' hawker in Srinagar.jpg|thumb|Charcoal barbecue in Srinagar.]]

One version of the origin of kababs is the one in which Turkish soldiers were first known to grill chunks of meat on open fires.<ref name="Bhowmik-2021">{{cite web |last1=Bhowmik |first1=Samarpan |title=One chef, one recipe: Kashmiri Kebab by Chef Ghulam Rabbani |url=https://www.traveldine.com/one-chef-one-recipe-kashmiri-kebab-by-chef-ghulam-rabbani/ |website=Traveldine.com |date=15 March 2021 |access-date=8 April 2022 |archive-date=5 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705030757/https://www.traveldine.com/one-chef-one-recipe-kashmiri-kebab-by-chef-ghulam-rabbani/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Kashmir's kababs are cooked with local spices and accompanied with dips:<ref name="Bhowmik-2021"/>

* ''Kabab'', condimented minced meat, roasted or fried, on skewers.<ref name="Kilam1991">{{cite book |last1=Kaul Kilam |first1=Shyam Rani |title=Culinary Art of Kashmir (Kashmiri Cookbook) |publisher=De Leij |date=1988}}</ref> According to chef Ghulam Nabi Dar (aka ''Bitte Waaze''), the meat for the kabab is first minced with a very sharp knife (''haché au couteau''), then it requires an egg, cumin, cardamom and garlic, then it needs to be minced some more until it becomes a paste, then it is mounted on 1 m long skewers to be reheated the day after.
*  ''Kokur kabab'', chicken kebab.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Razdan |first1=Sarla |title=Kashmiri Cuisine Through the Ages |date=2020 |publisher=Roli Books |location=New Delhi |isbn=978-81-941109-4-1 |page=138}}</ref>
* ''Lahradar kabab'', also known as ''lahabi/moachi'' kabab. Minced mutton classically shaped like a boat with a depression in the centre, cooked in curd based mild spicy gravy. Once softened, the meat is soaked overnight in egg and at least nine different seasonings and spices, including onions, red chili powder, nutmeg, garam masala, ginger, garlic and coriander. It is typically served with yoghurt.<ref name="Big Night in Kashmir">{{cite web |last1=Crowell |first1=Maddy |title=Big Night in Kashmir |url=https://explorepartsunknown.com/punjab/kashmir-eid/ |website=Explore Parts Unknown |date=4 April 2017 |access-date=25 June 2022}}</ref><ref name="Kashmiri Kitchen-2021">{{cite web |last1=Kashmiri Kitchen Restaurant |title=Kashmiri Kitchen Restaurant Menu |url=https://www.eazydiner.com/delhi-ncr/kashmiri-kitchen-mg-road-delhi-112140/menu |website=Kashmiri Kitchen (Easy Diner) |access-date=23 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=ROASTED KOFTA-KEBABS IN A RICH GRAVY |url=https://theculinarykashmiri.com/roasted-kofta-kebabs-in-a-rich-gravy/ |website=The Culinary Kashmiri |date=20 January 2021 |access-date=10 April 2022 |author1=Kashmiri }}</ref>
*  ''Kokur lahabdar kabab ruwangan'', chicken kebabs in rich tomato gravy.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Waza & Mohan |first1=Sharief, Shafi and Rafiq, & Rocky |title=Traditional Kashmiri Cuisine Wazwaan |date=2019 |publisher=Lustre Press Roli Books |location=New Delhi |isbn=978-81-941109-3-4 |page=56}}</ref>
* ''Shammi kabab'', wazwan style mutton patties with ground chickpeas, egg and mild Kashmiri spices.<ref name="Kashmiri Kitchen-2021"/><ref name="Zomato-2022">{{cite web |title=Sarposh Menu |url=https://www.zomato.com/bangalore/sarposh-indiranagar-bangalore/order |website=Zomato |access-date=19 March 2022}}</ref>
*  ''Champ'', lamb chops.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Razdan |first1=Sarla |title=Kashmiri Cuisine Through the Ages |date=2020 |publisher=Roli Books |location=New Delhi |isbn=978-81-941109-4-1 |page=52}}</ref>
*  ''Nadur maund'', Kashmir's answer to [[hash browns]], lotus root ginger and mint patties with a dash of eclectic Kashmiri spices.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pandita |first1=Nirtika |title=A Slice of Heaven |url=https://www.asianage.com/life/food/281118/a-slice-of-heaven.html |website=The Asian Age |date=28 November 2018 |access-date=26 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Nyenya-batta, menu |url=https://www.nyenya-batta.com/menu/ |website=Nyenya Batta Authentic Kashmiri Food |access-date=18 March 2022}}</ref>
*  ''Buzith Tsaman''{{Efn|The Ts represents the voiceless alveolar affricate sound {{IPAslink|t͡s|audio=Kashmiri pronunciation of ژ.ogg}}, which corresponds to the Kashmiri letter ژ.}}, grilled paneer marinated in yoghurt, cream and aniseed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chimra |first=Jigyasa Kapoor |title=Valley of spices |url=https://m.tribuneindia.com/2012/20120205/ttlife1.htm |access-date=27 May 2023 |website=m.tribuneindia.com |archive-date=29 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230929050704/https://m.tribuneindia.com/2012/20120205/ttlife1.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> It is said a poet wandering in the lovely forests of Kashmir, cooked this dish out in the open.<ref>{{cite web |title=Indian Durbar |website=UpperCrust |url=https://uppercrustindia.com/2019/posts/297/indian-durbar-bangalore }}</ref>
*  ''Buzith gaad'', charcoal grilled fish marinated with Kashmiri spices.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chef Shiveta Raina Kaul |url=https://knosh.in/chef/217?section=17 |website=Knosh.in |access-date=18 March 2022 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
*  ''Buzith olav, thool, maaz etc.'', the round oven-baked clay-pot ''kangir'' works as an oven for baking food-items such as eggs, potatoes, pea beans, chunks of meat etc.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dubey |first1=Kavya |title=The inevitable Kang'ir! |url=https://thekashmirwalla.com/the-inevitable-kangir/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211004094600/https://thekashmirwalla.com/the-inevitable-kangir/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=4 October 2021 |website=thekashmirwalla.com |date=26 February 2020 |access-date=4 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Bhat |first1=Riyaz |title=Kangir, savior of Kashmiris in bone chilling winter. |url=https://www.risingkashmir.com/Kangir--savior-of-Kashmiris-in-bone-chilling-winter-89270 |website=risingkashmir.com |access-date=4 October 2021 |archive-date=4 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211004094600/https://www.risingkashmir.com/Kangir--savior-of-Kashmiris-in-bone-chilling-winter-89270 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*  ''Talith gaad'', fish marinated in black pepper, cumin and Kashmiri chilli and then shallow-fried.<ref>{{cite web |title=Flavours of Kashmir at Vedic Village |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/culture/flavours-of-kashmir-at-vedic-village/cid/1379480 |website=The Telegraph Online |access-date=18 March 2022}}</ref>
*  ''Gaad talith ta badaam'', fried fish with almonds.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Razdan |first1=Sarla |title=Kashmiri Cuisine Through the Ages |date=2020 |publisher=Roli Books |location=New Delhi |isbn=978-81-941109-4-1 |page=21}}</ref>
*  ''Talith kokur'', Fried chicken.
* ''[[Tujj|Tujji]]'', meat marinated in Kashmiri red chillies and aniseed powder, then barbequed.<ref>{{cite web |last1=News Glory |title=Origin of Kashmir Tujj or Seekh Tujj |url=https://newsglory.in/origin-of-kashmir-tujj-or-seekh-tujj/ |website=News Glory |access-date=23 September 2021 |archive-date=15 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211015224758/https://newsglory.in/origin-of-kashmir-tujj-or-seekh-tujj/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Kaur |first1=Jasmine |title=Tujji Chicken: The Wazwani Dish that is Disappearing From the Culinary Scape |url=https://www.slurrp.com/article/tujji-chicken--the-wazwani-dish-that-is-disappearing-from-the-culinary-scape-1628674051368 |website=slurrp.com |access-date=22 October 2021}}</ref><ref name=Kilam1991/>
*  ''Gaad tujji'', fish kababs.
*  ''Tsaaman tujji'', Kashmiri style marinated cottage cheese chunks barbecued on a skewer and served with a side of chutney.<ref name="Zomato-2022"/>
*  ''Tshaap''{{Efn|The trigraph Tsh represents Ts aspirated counterpart {{IPAslink|t͡sʰ|audio=Kashmiri pronunciation of ژھ.wav}}, which corresponds to the Kashmiri letter ژھ.}} ''maaz'', sausages.<ref name=Reshii00>{{cite web |last1=Reshii |first1=Marryam H. |title=Kashmiri Dishes That are Fast Disappearing from the Valley |url=https://food.ndtv.com/food-drinks/kashmiri-dishes-that-are-fast-disappearing-from-the-valley-1457606 |website=NDTV Food |access-date=23 September 2021}}</ref>
*  ''Kaleeng'', thick membrane that covers sheep's head, skull and all, chopped coarsely and set to cook with spices and minimal liquid over a low fire for hours.<ref name=Reshii00/>

== Breakfast ==

For the average Kashmiri, breakfast normally means fresh bread from the local bakery and a cup of ''noon chai'' (salt tea).<ref name=livemint>{{cite web |last1=Mukherjee |first1=Sugato |title=Keep warm in Kashmir with this breakfast of champions |url=https://www.livemint.com/mint-lounge/features/keep-warm-in-kashmir-with-this-breakfast-of-champions-1549264883567.html |website=Livemint |date=4 February 2019 |access-date=8 April 2022}}</ref> While the bread is there in all the seasons for the breakfast, its accompaniments change.<ref name="Kaul-2023">{{Cite web |last=Kaul |first=Prof Upendra |date=4 December 2023 |title=Come Winter and Come our Special Cuisine |url=https://www.greaterkashmir.com/editorial-page-2/come-winter-and-come-our-special-cuisine/ |access-date=8 February 2024 |website=Greater Kashmir |language=en-US}}</ref> Some affordable luxuries include:

[[File:The Great Kashmiri Salt tea.png|thumb|Kashmiri noon chai.]]

* ''[[Harisse|Harisa]]'', made by specialised cooks called ''harisaguyr'', ''Harisa'' is a popular meat preparation made for breakfast, it is slow cooked with spices in a special underground oven for a 24-hour period and hand stirred.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shenoy |first1=Sanjana |title=This Kashmiri Chef is Preserving the art of Mutton Harissa in Srinagar |website=Curlytales |date=18 November 2021 |url=https://curlytales.com/this-kashmiri-chef-is-preserving-the-art-of-mutton-harissa-in-srinagar-heres-how/ }}</ref><ref name="Kaul-2023" /> A good ''harisa'' entails a meticulous mincing of deboned mutton, mixed with local rice, fennel seeds, cinnamon, cardamom and salt.<ref name="livemint" /> Cooked on sim fire for at least 6 to 8 hours, boiling smoky mustard oil and some milk is poured while the wooden masher continues to stir.<ref name="Kaul-2023" /> Small kebabs are made to be served along with and also a small serving of Methi (lamb's intestines cooked in fenugreek) and tempered onion rings.<ref name="Kaul-2023" /> In legend, an 18th century Afghan governor found the food so tasty he ate himself to death.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ahmed |first1=F |title=Eating it the Kashmiri way |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/eating-it-the-kashmiri-way/story-iER5zKGwYoqi9AT6YK2TKL.html |website=Hindustan Times |date=2 December 2006 |access-date=14 June 2022}}</ref>
* ''Harisa zafrani'', sprinkled with Kashmiri saffron. A maker in Aali Kadal was known for this peculiar dish.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shah |first1=Tariq |title=Harissa shops have started making the winter dish in Kashmir |url=https://voiceofvalley.com/2020/10/12/harissa-shops-have-started-making-the-winter-dish-in-kashmir/ |website=Voice of Valley |date=12 October 2020 |access-date=17 May 2022}}</ref>
* ''Luchi & halwa'', by luchi makers outside Kheer Bhawani shrine.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bamzai |first1=Kaveree |title=Why should Kashmiri Pandits return to sponsored lives in government dollhouses? |url=https://www.dailyo.in/politics/kashmiri-pandits-mufti-mohammed-sayeed-srinagar-kheer-bhawani-yasin-malik/story/1/3064.html |website=daily O |access-date=13 June 2022}}</ref>
* ''Makai vath'', cooked granular [[maize]] meal.<ref name="Culinary Art of Kashmir">{{cite book |last1=Kilam |first1=Shyam Rani & S.S Kaul |title=Culinary Art of Kashmir |date=1991 |publisher=De Leij |location=New Delhi |page=35}}</ref> Used to be a staple food in the unirrigated highland villages, where rice could not be grown.<ref name="Culinary Art of Kashmir" />
*  ''Gaer vugra'', [[water chestnut]] flour porridge. These water chestnuts or buffalo nuts are called ''gaer'' in Kashmiri.<ref name="Culinary Art of Kashmir" /> They grow in shallow waters at many places, especially near the shore of the famous Wular lake.<ref name="Culinary Art of Kashmir" /> In India, these water chestnuts also grow but are generally bigger in size and have more water content.<ref name="Culinary Art of Kashmir" /> Generally eaten with churned yoghurt diluted with water (''gurus'').<ref name="Culinary Art of Kashmir" />
*  ''Vushki vath'', barley meal porridge.<ref name="ReferenceJ">{{cite book |last1=Kilam |first1=Shyam Rani & S.S Kaul |title=Culinary Art of Kashmir |date=1991 |publisher=De Leij |location=New Delhi |page=36}}</ref> Cooked as a staple food in some hilly villages of Kashmir, where rice or maize is not easily available or grown.<ref name="ReferenceJ" />

== Wazwan dishes ==
[[File:TabakMaaz wazwan.jpg|thumb|Tabakhmaaz.]]
[[File:Kashmiri Aab Gosht.jpg|thumb|''Aab Gosh''.]]

Unlike most dishes of the Indian subcontinent where the flavour is added to the food while cooking on the flames, the wazwan flavours are added while the dish is still uncooked by adding flavoured water to the preparation or soaking in flavoured water (osmosis):<ref name="Times of India-2021">{{cite news |title=The classic tale of royal Kashmiri Wazwan |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/life-style/food-news/the-classic-tale-of-royal-kashmiri-wazwan/articleshow/87685773.cms |newspaper=The Times of India |date=14 November 2021 |access-date=9 April 2022}}</ref>

* ''Tabakhmaaz'', rib racks in ghee with sweet fat lodged between lacquered slips of meat<ref>{{cite web |title=Ahad Waza Kashmiri Wazwan Tabak Maaz (Fried Lamb Ribs) 500 gm |url=https://www.hamiast.com/ahad-waza/ahad-waza-kashmiri-wazwan-tabak-maaz-fried-lamb-ribs-500-gm |website=Hamiast |access-date=10 October 2021}}</ref> Kashmiri Hindus commonly refer to this dish as ''Qabargah''. It seems to have travelled from Kazakhstan where it is known by its Pandit name, ''Qabargah''.<ref name="Excelsior-2023">{{Cite web |last=Excelsior |first=Daily |date=4 February 2023 |title=Cuisines of Kashmir: A tradition and a treasure trove |url=https://www.dailyexcelsior.com/cuisines-of-kashmir-a-tradition-and-a-treasure-trove/ |access-date=8 October 2023 |website=Jammu Kashmir Latest News {{!}} Tourism {{!}} Breaking News J&K |language=en-US}}</ref> While ''Qabargah'' is simmered on a low heat for a longer duration and then fried very quickly, ''Tabakhmaaz'' is boiled with salt and garlic and characterised by a slightly elastic texture.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pallab |title=Koshur Saal by ITC Kakatiya Showcases the beauty of Kashmiri Pandit Cuisine |url=https://www.hydfoodguy.com/kashmiri-pandit-cuisine-hyderabad-itc-kakatiya/Excelsior-2023#:~:text=Kabargah%20is%20the%20Pandit%20version,and%20then%20fried%20very%20quickly. |website=HydFoodGuy.com |date=21 July 2018 |access-date=19 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Nabi |first1=Safina |title=Meet the 'Devil Chefs' of Kashmir |url=https://www.atlasobscura.com/articles/devil-chefs-of-kashmir |website=Gastro Obscura |date=4 February 2022 |access-date=19 March 2022}}</ref>
*  ''Tang ta lahabi kabab'', whole Kashmiri pears and mutton kababs that often go with a tomato-yoghurt gravy.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lahabi Kebab Recipe |url=https://recipes.timesofindia.com/recipes/lahabi-kebab/rs63814549.cms |website=Times Food |access-date=15 October 2021}}</ref>
* ''Waaza kokur'', whole chicken cooked in saffron gravy with mild Kashmiri spices.<ref name="Kashmiri Kitchen-2021"/>
*  ''Safed kokur'', chicken with white sauce.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wazwan |url=https://budgam.nic.in/culinary-delight/wazwan/ |website=District Budgam, Jammu and Kashmir |access-date=30 September 2021}}</ref>
*  [[File:Daniphol wazwan.jpg|thumb|Dani Phoul.]]''Dani phoul'', mutton shank.
*  ''Aab gosh'', also known as ''dodhe maaz''. A famous milk-based curry cooked in spices and ghee over a low flame.<ref>{{Cite web |title=5 Delicious Kashmiri Dishes We Ought to be Thankful For {{!}} LBB |url=https://lbb.in/delhi/5-delicious-kashmiri-dishes-we-ought-to-be-thankful-for/ |access-date=10 March 2022 |website=LBB, Delhi-NCR |language=en}}</ref> Ten litres of pure cow milk is reduced to one and then mixed with the mutton.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bakhsh |first1=Zenaira |title=The origin, evolution of Kashmir's emblematic cuisine Wazwan |url=https://thekashmirwalla.com/the-origin-evolution-of-kashmirs-emblematic-cuisine-wazwan/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920071748/https://thekashmirwalla.com/the-origin-evolution-of-kashmirs-emblematic-cuisine-wazwan/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=20 September 2021 |website=The Kashmir Walla |date=15 July 2021 |access-date=10 May 2022}}</ref>
*  ''Methi maaz'', mutton intestines flavoured with a spice mixture containing dried fenugreek (''methi'') leaves.<ref>{{cite web |title=Methi Maaz |url=http://kashmirizaiqa.com/product/methi-maaz-250-grms/ |website=Kashmiri Zaika |access-date=28 September 2021 |archive-date=28 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210928053437/http://kashmirizaiqa.com/product/methi-maaz-250-grms/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*  ''Waazeh hedar'', Kashmiri wazwan-style mushrooms.
*  ''Martswangan kormeh'', meat cooked with spices and yogurt and mostly using Kashmiri red chillies and hot in taste.
*  ''Kokur martsawangan kormeh'', Chicken cooked in red hot chilly gravy.<ref name="Kashmiri Kitchen-2021"/>
*  ''Aloobukhar kormeh'', mince cooked with dried plums.<ref name="Kashmiri Kitchen-2021"/>
*  ''Badam kormeh'', tender mutton pieces cooked in creamy almond gravy.<ref name="scribd-2021">{{cite web |title=Ahadsons Foods (Menu) |url=https://www.scribd.com/document/91203965/Menu-of-Kashmiri-Food |website=scribd.com |access-date=30 September 2021}}</ref>
*  ''Danival kormeh'' lamb cooked with coriander or parsley.
* ''Kokur danival kormeh'', chicken cooked in curd based gravy, flavoured with saffron and fresh coriander.<ref name="Kashmiri Kitchen-2021"/>
*  ''Monje kael'', knol-khol prepared in onion gravy.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Waza & Mohan |first1=Shareif, Shafi, and Rafiq & Rocky |title=Wazwan Traditional Kashmiri Cuisine |date=2019 |publisher=Lustre Press Roli Books |location=New Delhi |isbn=978-81-941109-3-4}}</ref>

*  ''Tshatt/maaz rass'', mutton stock with mutton pieces flavoured with aromatic spices and salt.<ref>{{cite web |title=Poush Essence of Kashmir (Menu) |url=https://www.zomato.com/mumbai/poush-essence-of-kashmir-kurla/menu |website=zomato.com |access-date=30 September 2021}}</ref>
*  ''Channa rass'', easily made chickpea soup.<ref>{{cite web |title=Easy Chickpea Soup – Instant Pot Kashmiri Chana Soup |url=https://fastcurries.com/2021/02/22/easy-chickpea-soup-instant-pot-kashmiri-chana-soup/ |website=Fastcurries.com |date=22 February 2021 |access-date=15 June 2022}}</ref>

== Domestic meat stews ==
[[File:Shabdeg Main Ingredients.JPG|thumb|''Shab deg'', the Kashmiri ''pot-au-feu'']]
*  [[File:Shabdeg1.jpg|thumb|''Shab Deg'' with chunks.]] [[File:Shabdeg..JPG|thumb|Shab Deg with Meatballs.]] [[File:Rogan josh02.jpg|thumb|''[[Rogan josh]]'']] [[File:Yakhni from kashmir.jpg|thumb|Yakhein.]] [[File:Shaljam Gosht (Shalgam Gosht).JPG|thumb|Gogjee Ta Maaz (Mutton with Turnips).]]''Qaliya'', a mutton delicacy in which all flavours are included, excluding red chilly powder.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chowdhary |first1=Diksha |title=Taste of Kashmir |url=https://www.dailyexcelsior.com/taste-of-kashmir/ |website=dailyexcelsior.com |date=28 August 2021 |access-date=5 October 2021}}</ref>
*  ''Kokur qaliya'', chicken ''qaliya''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Razdan |first1=Sarla |title=Kashmiri Cuisine Through the Ages |date=2020 |publisher=Roli Books |location=New Delhi |isbn=978-81-941109-4-1 |page=135}}</ref>
* [[Shab Deg]]: dish cooked with turnip and meat/duck/chicken/beef and balls of ground meat, left to simmer overnight.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.khanapakana.com/recipe/766d440d-9da7-4c57-aa4e-dfda3e333ed4/kashmiri-meat-shabdeg|title=Kashmiri Meat Shabdeg - khanaPakana.com|website=www.khanapakana.com|access-date=1 January 2017|archive-date=26 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161126194748/http://www.khanapakana.com/recipe/766d440d-9da7-4c57-aa4e-dfda3e333ed4/kashmiri-meat-shabdeg|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Ahmed-2006">{{cite web |last1=Ahmed |first1=F |title=Eating it the Kashmiri Way |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/eating-it-the-kashmiri-way/story-iER5zKGwYoqi9AT6YK2TKL.html |website=Hindustantimes.com |date=2 December 2006 |access-date=30 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Mushtaq |first1=Tasavur |title=Forgotten Shab Daig |url=https://kashmirlife.net/forgotten-shab-daig-133280/ |website=kashmirlife.net |date=23 February 2017 |access-date=30 September 2021}}</ref><ref name="Nabi-2016">{{cite web |last1=Nabi |first1=Nabeena |title=These are the Must-Try Traditional Kashmiri Winter Foods |url=https://www.gyawun.com/these-are-the-must-try-traditional-kashmiri-winter-foods/ |website=Gyawun.com |date=28 December 2016 |access-date=4 October 2021}}</ref>
*  ''Dani'', marrow-bone in gravy.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Mattoo |first1=Neerja |title=Sal: A Feast of Kashmiri Cuisine |date=2008 |publisher=Gulshan Books |location=Srinagar |isbn=978-81-8339-063-7 |page=21}}</ref>
*  ''Matshgand'', lamb meatballs in a gravy tempered with red chillies. A lot of emphasis is put on the shape of the meat (oblong and not round) and the colour of the gravy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mutton Masch (meatballs) |url=https://www.orzookitchen.com/mutton-masch-meatballs.html |access-date=15 February 2024 |website=ORZOO |language=en |archive-date=15 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240215105434/https://www.orzookitchen.com/mutton-masch-meatballs.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*  ''Methi matsh'', muttonballs with fenugreek leaves that have been boiled, crushed or liquidised into a paste.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Khosa |first1=Nancy |title=Kashmiri Cuisine Saffron Plate A Historic Perspective |date=2016 |publisher=Utpal Publications |location=Delhi |isbn=978-81-85217-34-5 |page=109}}</ref>
*  ''Matsh ta tser'', lamb fingers with apricot.<ref name="ReferenceK">{{cite book |last1=Razdan |first1=Sarla |title=Kashmiri Cuisine Through the Ages |date=2020 |publisher=Roli Books |location=New Delhi |isbn=978-81-941109-4-1 |page=30}}</ref> The dish looks beautiful when laid on the table as the apricots remain yellow and the minced meat red making it very colourful.<ref name="ReferenceK" />

== Meatballs ==
The ''wazas'' are trained for years to learn techniques for making cuts and grinding meat.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bakhsh |first1=Zenaira |title=The origin, evolution of Kashmir's emblematic cuisine Wazwan |url=https://thekashmirwalla.com/the-origin-evolution-of-kashmirs-emblematic-cuisine-wazwan/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920071748/https://thekashmirwalla.com/the-origin-evolution-of-kashmirs-emblematic-cuisine-wazwan/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=20 September 2021 |website=Kashmir Walla |date=15 July 2021 |access-date=8 April 2022}}</ref> Traditionally, the lamb is mashed with walnut wood:<ref name="In search Wazwan">{{cite web |last1=Jolly |first1=Surjan Singh |title=In search Wazwan |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/culture/food/in-search-wazwan/cid/1839845 |website=The Telegraph online |access-date=8 May 2022}}</ref>[[File:Rista wazwan.jpg|thumb|Riste.]]
*  ''Goshtabeh''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://recipes.timesofindia.com/recipes/goshtaba/rs61764953.cms|title=Goshtaba Recipe: How to Make Goshtaba Recipe | Homemade Goshtaba Recipe|website=recipes.timesofindia.com}}</ref> minced mutton balls with spices in yogurt gravy. Also known as 'The Dish of Kings' in Kashmir region and the last dish of the banquet.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dutta |first1=Ayandrali |title=The Story Of Exotic Kashmiri Gushtaba |url=https://www.slurrp.com/article/the-story-of-exotic-kashmiri-gushtaba-1645032501594 |website=Slurrp.com |access-date=8 April 2022}}</ref> Jawaharlal Nehru once named it 'the cashmere of meats'.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 September 1987 |title=KASHMIRI CUISINE OFFERS A DELICATELY SPICED, SAFFRON-SPANGLED |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1987/09/03/kashmiri-cuisine-offers-a-delicately-spiced-saffron-spangled/ |access-date=14 February 2024 |website=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> The Bollywood actor Yusuf Khan aka Dilip Kumar was said to love ''goshtabeh'' the most.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gul |first1=Khaled |title=Dilip Kumar relished Kashmiri Wazwan, loved Gushtaba the most |url=https://www.greaterkashmir.com/todays-paper/kashmir-todays-paper/dilip-kumar-relished-kashmiri-wazwan-loved-gushtaba-the-most |website=Greater Kashmir |date=8 July 2021 |access-date=11 May 2022}}</ref> In December 1955, Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad, the then Prime Minister of Jammu and Kashmir and Nikita S. Khurschev, the first secretary of the Soviet Communist party were photographed feeding each other ''goshtabeh''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ganai |first1=Naseer |title=Why Kashmir's Famed Wazwan Is Always On The Diplomacy Menu |url=https://www.outlookindia.com/national/why-kashmir-s-famed-wazwan-is-always-on-the-diplomacy-menu-news-193258 |website=Outlook India |date=26 April 2022 |access-date=17 May 2022}}</ref>

* ''Beef goshtabeh''.<ref name="Reshii-2021a">{{cite web |last1=Reshii |first1=Marryam |title=City on the plate: Srinagar |url=https://marryamhreshii.com/whats-cooking-in-kashmir/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170108224853/http://marryamhreshii.com/whats-cooking-in-kashmir/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=8 January 2017 |website=Marryam H Reshii Food, Travel, People... |access-date=25 September 2021}}</ref> Pulverised beef with 25 per cent fat is pounded into a pulpy mass and seasoned before being shaped into meatballs.<ref name="Quraishi-2023">{{Cite web |last=Quraishi |first=Faisal |date=22 October 2023 |title=EPICURIOUS: TREATS FROM KASHMIR |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1782210 |access-date=22 October 2023 |website=DAWN.COM |language=en}}</ref> It is then immersed in a seasoned hot water bath, before being placed in a bubbling-hot broth of well-churned yoghurt, laced with milk and some beef stock and cooked to a semi-thick consistency.<ref name="Quraishi-2023" /> The original recipe calls for very fatty buffalo meat.<ref name="Quraishi-2023" />

== Mushrooms ==
[[File:Morchella esculenta grouping 01.jpg|thumb|The much-prized ''kanaguchhi'' (''[[Morchella esculenta]]'')]] 
Native to the Himalayan foothills, ''Guchhi'' or ''kanaguchhi'' mushrooms (species in the genus ''[[Morchella]]'', commonly known as ''morels'' elsewhere) are highly prized in Kashmir . With the exception of a few very limited and experimental successes, efforts to [[Fungiculture|cultivate]] ''(kana)guchhi'' or ''morels'' at a large scale have been unsuccessful and consumption relies on the harvest of wild mushrooms.<ref>{{Cite report |url=https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/26906 |title=Ecology and management of morels harvested from the forests of western North America. |last1=Pilz |first1=David |last2=McLain |first2=Rebecca |date=2007 |publisher=U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service, Pacific Northwest Research Station |issue=PNW-GTR-710 |doi=10.2737/pnw-gtr-710 |location=Portland, OR |language=en |last3=Alexander |first3=Susan |last4=Villarreal-Ruiz |first4=Luis |last5=Berch |first5=Shannon |last6=Wurtz |first6=Tricia L. |last7=Parks |first7=Catherine G. |last8=McFarlane |first8=Erika |last9=Baker |first9=Blaze|url-access=subscription }}</ref> <ref>{{Cite news |title=Gucchi: Foraging for world's most expensive mushroom in Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/travel/destinations/gucchi-foraging-for-worlds-most-expensive-mushroom-in-kashmir-himachal-pradesh/articleshow/102900013.cms |access-date=27 October 2024 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

== ''Tsaaman'' ==
[[Paneer]] is called T''saaman'' in Kashmiri.<ref name="sbs.com.au">{{cite web |last1=Kamini |first1=Sarina |title=Frying paneer is a Kashmiri cooking tradition – and it's delicious |url=https://www.sbs.com.au/food/article/2021/09/06/frying-paneer-kashmiri-cooking-tradition-and-its-delicious |website=SBS |access-date=20 May 2023}}</ref> The spicing falls into the sweet-savoury spectrum which means using a lot of cinnamon, mace and clove alongside earthier spices like cumin seed and ground coriander.<ref name="sbs.com.au"/>  The scarcity of fresh ginger in mountain geography also means that ground ginger is a spice staple.<ref name="sbs.com.au"/> Paneer recipes are:

== Fish ==

The practice of shadow fishing is locally known as ''Tshaayi Gaad'' in Anchar lake in the Soura vicinity of Srinagar city.<ref name="Bhat-2024">{{Cite web |last=Bhat |first=Muzamil |date=28 January 2024 |title=Kashmir: Fishermen in Anchar lake brace up for 'shadow fishing' |url=https://www.siasat.com/kashmir-fishermen-in-anchar-lake-brace-up-for-shadow-fishing-2966025/ |access-date=8 February 2024 |website=The Siasat Daily |language=en-US}}</ref> Fishermen row their boats early in the morning, breaking the frozen part of the lake to catch fish with a harpoon.<ref name="Bhat-2024" /> They create a shadow on the nook of their boat by hiding themselves under a blanket or a makeshift umbrella made of straw to attract the fish and later strike the approaching fish with the harpoon.<ref name="Bhat-2024" />  The banks of the lake of yore used to be dotted with thickets of willow trees under whose shadow the fish would take refuge during summers, thereby easing the task for the local fishermen to catch them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dhar |first=Debi |date=10 February 2021 |title=In Pictures: Traditional Shadow Fishing Returns to Kashmir's Anchar Lake As Mercury Rises |url=https://www.greaterkashmir.com/photos/traditional-shadow-fishing-returns-to-kashmirs-anchar-lake-as-mercury-rises/ |access-date=8 February 2024 |website=Greater Kashmir |language=en-US}}</ref> Common fish dishes are:

*  ''Nader ti Gaad'', fish (''Bilose'', ''Zob'',<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nabi |first1=Daanish Bin |title=Kashmir: Where There's No One to Fish for |url=https://www.newsclick.in/Kashmir-Where-There-One-Fish |website=newsclick.in |date=22 October 2019 |access-date=4 October 2021}}</ref> ''Indian Major Carp'', ''Catla'', ''Rohu'', ''Margarita'', ''Mahseer'',<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bhat |first1=Saima |title=In the Net |url=https://kashmirlife.net/in-the-net-issue-48-vol-07-96934/ |website=kashmirlife.net |date=16 February 2016 |access-date=4 October 2021}}</ref> ''Snow Trout'', ''Niger'', ''Chush'', ''Khront'', ''Churu'' etc.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Najar |first1=Naveed Ahmad |title=The great highland fishes of Kashmir, gone forever in the abyss of human depradation |url=https://kashmirreader.com/2021/01/20/the-great-highland-fishes-of-kashmir-gone-forever-in-the-abyss-of-human-depredation/ |website=Kashmir Reader |date=20 January 2021 |access-date=4 October 2021}}</ref>) cooked with lotus stem, a delicacy cooked on festival days like Eid, Navroze and Gaadi Batti (Festival of Kashmiri Pandits).
*  ''Mujh Gaad'', a dish of radishes with a choice of fish.
* ''Haak Gaad'', Fish curry cooked with kashmiri spinach.<ref name="Kashmiri Kitchen-2021"/>
* ''Gada Ta Gogjee/Monjje/Band Gupi'', Fish cooked with Turnips, or Knol Khol, or Cabbage.<ref name=Kilam1991/>
*  ''Gaad Ta Tsounth'', fish cooked with green apples.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Razdan |first1=Sarla |title=Kashmiri Cuisine Through the Ages |date=2020 |publisher=Roli Books |location=New Delhi |isbn=978-81-941109-4-1 |page=64}}</ref>
*  ''Gaad Qaliya'', fish in yellow gravy.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Razdan |first1=Sarla |title=Kashmiri Cuisine Through the Ages |date=2020 |publisher=Roli Books |location=New Delhi |isbn=978-81-941109-4-1 |page=143}}</ref>
*  ''Ruwangan/Tamatar Gaad'', white river fish cooked delicately in a tomato gravy.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Waza & Mohan |first1=Sharief, Shafi and Rafiq, & Rocky |title=Traditional Kashmiri Cuisine Wazwaan |date=2019 |publisher=Lustre Press Roli Books |location=New Delhi |isbn=978-81-941109-3-4 |page=52}}</ref>

*  ''Gaad Leij'', trout fish cooked in traditional Kashmiri style and served with vegetables such as ''nadur'', etc.<ref>{{cite web |title=Menu of Kashmir Trout, Rainawari |url=https://www.zomato.com/srinagar/kashmir-trout-rainawari/menu |website=Zomato |access-date=20 May 2023}}</ref>

* ''Fari/Phari'', smoked fish.<ref name=Kilam1991/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Asif |first1=Umer |title=Kashmir's winter delicacy: Smoked Fish |url=https://thekashmirwalla.com/kashmirs-winter-delicacy-smoked-fish/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210925042313/https://thekashmirwalla.com/kashmirs-winter-delicacy-smoked-fish/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=25 September 2021 |website=Kashmir Walla |date=13 December 2020 |access-date=25 September 2021}}</ref> A winter delicacy prepared in a particular method by only a few remaining households in Srinagar's Tiploo Mohalla.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mattoo |first1=Abrar |title=A mix of nourishment, nutrition and nuance |url=https://www.risingkashmir.com/A-mix-of-nourishment--nutrition-and-nuance-98232 |website=Rising Kashmir |date=3 January 2022 |access-date=19 March 2022 |archive-date=18 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220318103051/https://www.risingkashmir.com/A-mix-of-nourishment--nutrition-and-nuance-98232 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The fish used is a variety of trout belonging to the genus ''Schizothorax''.<ref name="lifestyle.livemint.com">{{cite web |last1=Nabi |first1=Safina |title=Why Kashmir's smoked fish dishes are vanishing from its cuisine |url=https://lifestyle.livemint.com/food/discover/why-kashmir-s-smoked-fish-dishes-are-vanishing-from-its-cuisine-111605680948975.html |website=Mint Lounge |date=18 November 2020 |access-date=11 May 2022}}</ref>
*  ''Phari Ta Haakh'', smoked fish with collard greens.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shabir |first1=Najwa |title=Delicious Kashmiri Recipe – Smoked Fish with Haak |url=https://khyenchyen.net/2018/12/07/delicious-recipe-smoked-fish-with-haak/ |website=Khyen Chyen |date=7 December 2018 |access-date=26 September 2021}}</ref> The skin of the smoked fish is removed and it is fried until it turns reddish-brown.<ref name="lifestyle.livemint.com"/> The fish is added to collard greens and cooked until all the water is absorbed and oil floats on top.<ref name="lifestyle.livemint.com"/> Best had with steamed rice, and best not to reheat the dish.<ref name="lifestyle.livemint.com"/>

== Game (''shikaar'') ==
[[File:Ducks on Lake Dal, Kashmir (8142492655).jpg|thumb|Ducks on Dal Lake.]]
An estimated 50-60 birds are killed every day in wetlands across Kashmir.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rashid |first1=Afshan |title=Following a poacher in the heart of Kashmir's wetlands |url=https://freepresskashmir.news/2017/05/09/following-a-poacher-in-the-heart-of-kashmirs-wetlands/ |website=Free Press Kashmir |date=9 May 2017 |access-date=16 June 2022}}</ref> Hunted game (''shikaar'') is not generally cooked immediately,<ref name="ReferenceU">{{cite book |last1=Khosa |first1=Nancy |title=Kashmiri Cuisine Saffron Plate A Historic Perspective |date=2016 |publisher=Utpal Publications |location=Delhi |isbn=978-81-85217-34-5 |page=125}}</ref> but hung for several days before being dressed. This step is understood to make the meat more tender.<ref name="ReferenceU"/>

In British India, ''markhor'' (screw horn goat) was considered to be among the most challenging game species.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ganaie |first=Nazir |date=25 April 2022 |title=Markhor{{!}}The Camouflaged Cliffhangers of Kashmir's Mountains |work=Greater Kashmir |url=https://www.greaterkashmir.com/life-style/markhorthe-camouflaged-cliffhangers-of-kashmirs-mountains |access-date=22 May 2023}}</ref> It is the largest wild goat in the world.<ref>{{Cite web |title=KASHMIR MARKHOR RECOVERY PROJECT |url=https://www.wti.org.in/projects/kashmir-markhor-recovery-project/ |access-date=22 May 2023 |website=WTI |language=en-US}}</ref> It is locally regarded as the tastiest wild meat.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Joshi |first=Swati |date=10 January 2022 |title=Hangul, Markhor, Snow Leopards: Kashmir's Most Targeted Species |url=https://kashmirobserver.net/2022/01/10/hangul-markhor-snow-leopards-kashmirs-most-targeted-species/ |access-date=22 May 2022}}</ref>

Indian wild boar was introduced in the Himalayan region by Maharaja Gulab Singh, a Dogra military general.<ref name="Ali-2023">{{Cite news |last=Ali |first=Jehangir |date=18 May 2023 |title=Outcry as wild boars reappear in Kashmir after decades |work=AlJazeera |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/5/18/outcry-as-wild-boars-reappear-in-kashmir-after-decades |access-date=22 May 2023}}</ref> Its meat was considered a great delicacy for the Dogras and Sikhs, but after 1947 its population started dwindling in the Muslim-majority region.<ref name="Ali-2023" />

Game dishes are:

*  ''Pacchin Dumpokhta'', pintail. Called the king of the winter cuisine in Kashmir, it is considered a delicacy and eaten by Kashmiri Pandits who would not normally eat chicken.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ganju |first1=Chandramukhi |title=Recipe Pacchin/Flying Bird |url=http://shehjar.net/list/113/1253/1.html |website=Shehjar |access-date=8 April 2022 }}{{Dead link|date=May 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref name="Kaul-2023" /> The migratory bird looks like a duck but can fly with great speed. It comes to wetlands of Kashmir during winter.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Mattoo |first1=Neerja |title=Sal: A Feast of Kashmiri Cuisine |date=2008 |publisher=Gulshan Books |location=Srinagar |isbn=978-81-8339-063-7 |page=78}}</ref> It is deep fried and cooked with hot spices.<ref name="Kaul-2023" /> The meat under the feathers is tough, but regarded by some as tasty and warming.<ref name="Kaul-2023" />
*  ''Batook Palak'', duck with spinach.<ref name="Ahmad-2021b"/>
*  ''Batook Ta Zamut Dodh'', duck in a curd curry.

It is winter comfort food in Kashmir.<ref name="Slurrp-2024" />
* ''Shikar Rogan Josh'', Roghan Josh of hunted game birds and animals such as mallard, geese, plover, snipe, rail, teal, quail, pintail, Wigeon, grouse, partridge, pheasant, spotted deer, hangal, antelope, wild goat etc.<ref name=Kilam1991/>
* ''Shikar Ta Nadeir'', meat of game birds cooked with lotus roots.<ref name=Kilam1991/>

== Cheese ==
The nomadic shepherds of the Kashmir valley, ''Gujjars'' and ''Bakerwals'' move their herd of dairy cattle and their own settlements up and down the mountains based on changing seasons:<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pal |first1=Sanchari |title=This Traditional Kashmiri Cheese Is One of the Most Unique in the World |url=https://www.thebetterindia.com/61166/kalari-cheese-kashmir/ |website=The Better India |date=11 July 2016 |access-date=9 April 2022}}</ref>

* ''Maesh Crari or Maesh Craji'',<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kashmiri Food Recipes |title=Kashmiri Food Recipes |url=http://www.kashmirifood.com/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040328011429/http://kashmirifood.com/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=28 March 2004 |access-date=23 September 2021}}</ref> described as ''the mozzarella of Kashmir''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pal |first1=Sanchari |title=This Traditional Kashmiri Cheese is one of the most Unique in the world |url=https://www.thebetterindia.com/61166/kalari-cheese-kashmir/ |website=thebetterindia.com |date=11 July 2016 |access-date=5 October 2021}}</ref> The discs are first coated with chilli, turmeric and salt, and then fried in mustard oil until they form a crisp, golden outer layer and the inside stays soft and creamy.<ref name="aljazeera.com">{{cite web |last1=Bhat |first1=Suhail |title=In search of Kashmir's nomadic delicacies |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2022/6/28/in-search-of-kashmirs-nomadic-delicacies |website=AlJazeera |access-date=7 August 2022}}</ref>
* ''Kudan'', a rare Gujjar goat cheese that looks like paneer but is more crumbly and akin to feta.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Halarnkar |first1=Samar |title=In search of the great Kashmiri meal |url=https://www.livemint.com/Leisure/9egjoApeyqkeqTHzLGkOGI/In-search-of-the-great-Kashmiri-meal.html |website=Livemint |date=27 May 2016 |access-date=9 April 2022}}</ref> Kudan is prepared in Bakerwal tents by heating some mustard oil in a pot on fire and then mixing some salt, turmeric and chilli along with the ''kudan'' cheese curds.<ref name="aljazeera.com"/> Everything melts together into a golden liquid flecked with red chilli and small nuggets of ''kudan''.<ref name="aljazeera.com"/>

== English pastry ==

Before 1918, Abdul Ahad Bhat, of Ahdoos, was under the tutelage of English bakers at Nedou's, a hotel in Srinagar owned by Austro-Swiss Michael Nedou.<ref name="Bread, butter and bakerkhani">{{cite web |last1=Wani |first1=Riyaz |title=Bread, butter and bakerkhani |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/blink/takeaway/bread-butter-and-bakerkhani/article9680745.ece |website=Hindu Business Line |date=5 May 2017 |access-date=13 June 2022}}</ref> He quickly picked up the art of baking, and started a small bakery, the first by a Kashmiri at that time.<ref name="Bread, butter and bakerkhani"/> Ahdoos's forte was English goodies, and as India inched towards freedom from British Rule he added Kashmiri items to the menu.<ref name="Bread, butter and bakerkhani"/> Mughal Darbar was established on Residency Road in 1984 and on the road parallel is Jee Enn, founded by Ghulam Nabi Sofi in 1972.<ref name="Bread, butter and bakerkhani"/> Many of the owners and staff of these new bakeries have trained in Ahdoos.<ref name="Bread, butter and bakerkhani"/> The variety of pastries include:

* ''Chicken or Mutton Patty'', meat seasoned with salt, pepper and garlic, encased in layered puff pastry.<ref name="Bread, butter and bakerkhani"/>
*  ''Puffs''.<ref name="Bread, butter and bakerkhani"/>
* ''Cream Rolls''.<ref name="Bread, butter and bakerkhani"/>

* ''Coconut Macaroons''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Charagi |first1=Nipa |title=A bag of quince from Kashmir |url=https://www.livemint.com/Leisure/vSEz8GOQQ2lpoILMIOJZBI/A-bag-of-quince-from-Kashmir.html |website=Livemint |date=7 October 2016 |access-date=14 June 2022}}</ref>

== Kandarwan ==
The Kashmir Valley is noted for its bakery tradition, that of the ''qKndarwan''. Nowhere else in the Indian subcontinent can be found such a huge variety of leavened breads, another pointer to the Central Asian influence on Kashmiris' food habits.<ref name="ReferenceA">{{cite book |last1=Mattoo |first1=Neerja |title=Sal: A Feast of Kashmiri Cuisine |date=2008 |publisher=Gulshan Books |location=Srinagar |isbn=978-81-8339-063-7 |page=13}}</ref> On the [[Dal Lake]] in Kashmir or in downtown Srinagar, bakery shops are elaborately laid out. Bakers sell various kinds of breads with golden brown crusts topped with sesame and poppy seeds.

Different kinds of traditional Kashmiri breads include:

* ''Tsoet'' and ''Tsoechvor/Tilvor'' are crisp and flaky small round breads topped with ''khaskhash'' (poppy) and ''til'' (sesame) seeds.<ref name="Gull-2019">{{Cite web |last=Gull |first=Murtaza |date=12 January 2019 |title=Into The Heart of Kashmir Culture- Kashmiri Bakery |url=https://thekashmiriyat.co.uk/into-the-heart-of-kashmir-culture-kashmiri-bakery/ |access-date=8 February 2024 |website=The Kashmiriyat}}</ref> A local bagel of about three inches diameter and six inches circumference, the upper half is soft and the lower crust is crispy.<ref name="Gull-2019" /> It is the evening/afternoon bread.<ref name="Gull-2019" />
* ''Sheermal'', a saffron flavoured traditional flatbread said to have originated in Iran.<ref name="risingkashmir-2024">{{Cite web |title=Sheermal: Crispy Kashmiri bread |url=https://risingkashmir.com/sheermal-crispy-kashmiri-bread- |access-date=8 February 2024 |website=risingkashmir.com}}</ref> It is offered in both sweet and flavourful versions.<ref name="risingkashmir-2024" /> The ''sheermal'' bread is usually dented with multiple patterns bordering on corresponding lines.<ref name="risingkashmir-2024" />
* ''Baqerkhayn'' (puff pastry), Kashmiri [[Bakarkhani|bakerkhani]] has a special place in Kashmiri cuisine. It is similar to a round naan in appearance, but crisp and layered, and sprinkled with sesame seeds.<ref>{{cite web |title=Culture of Anantnag |url=http://anantnag.nic.in/culture.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090619085207/http://anantnag.nic.in/culture.htm |archive-date=19 June 2009 |website=District Anantnag J&K}}</ref> It is typically consumed hot during breakfast.<ref>{{cite web |date=13 March 2008 |title=Kashmir has special confectionary |url=http://www.thaindian.com/newsportal/india-news/kashmir-has-special-confectionary_10027147.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180512112836/http://www.thaindian.com/newsportal/india-news/kashmir-has-special-confectionary_10027147.html |archive-date=12 May 2018 |access-date=18 July 2013 |publisher=Thaindian.com}}</ref>
* ''Lavasa'',  thin unleavened flat bread, white in colour, made of ''maida'' (finely-milled wheat flour).<ref name="Gull-2019" /> It is a paper-thin blistered naan.<ref name="Gull-2019" /> Some lavasas are soft while others are crispy.<ref name="Gull-2019" /> 
* ''Girda'', made with dough that has been fermented overnight, rolls of dough are flattened out by hand and finger impressions are pressed into it to give you lines that run down its length.<ref name="Gull-2019" /> ''Girda'' and ''lavas'' are served with butter.
* ''Kulcha'', baked exclusively with ghee, this small, hard, dry, crumbly bread, is usually round in shape.<ref name="Gull-2019" /> It is decorated by placing a peanut in the centre of the upper face.<ref name="Gull-2019" />
* ''Roth khabar'', a cake-like sweet bread made in traditional tandoor and covered with dry fruits.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tickoo |first=Sakshi |date=10 August 2022 |title=Kashmir: 5 Different Varieties Of Breads You Must Try |url=https://www.outlookindia.com/travel/kashmir-5-different-varieties-of-breads-you-must-try-news-214946 |access-date=8 February 2024 |work=Outlook}}</ref>
